cells.location: GUJARAT JUNAGADH DISTRICT PATAN VERAVAL TAHSIL Prabhās Pātan — Gujarat
cells.place: Copper-plate set deposited in the Museum. Impression from the Assistant Curator of the Museum. Findspot: Ambālikā, Junagadh District.
cells.remarks: Issued from Krishnanagara. Records the grant, made by the ruler, of two plots of land situated in Saurashtra, to the Uthēdālata to the Buddhist nunnery (Bhikkhu-sangha) in the vicinity of Uthēdāla. The gift was intended for the maintenance of the vihāra, for providing materials for the worship of the Buddha and for the feeding of members of the Bhikkhu-sangha. In characters of the 6th-7th century A.D. Published in J. O. I., Vol. XIX, pp. 279 ff., and Plate.

Also states that the gift was intended for the increase of the religious merit and fame of the king and his parents.

cells.remarks: Registers a royal grant of the village of Mattūru, renamed as Sālagrāma, situated in the district (valitā) of Āraga-Sāntalige and Daṇḍayaka-Hosaɓali, in the Gaṅgamandala-nāḍu of the Gjajānura-sthala of the Āraga-rājya. The donee was Tryaiṇ- haka, son of Hańge Tipparasa of the Āśvalāyana-sūtra; Kāśyapa-gōtra and Ṛik-śākhā. With reference to the same occasion the donee granted the village of Urukaduvilie to Harihara-ārādhya, the son of Mādhav-ārādhya of the Kōṭīśāna-sthla, Āpastamba-sūtra, Yajus-sūtra and Harit- sa-gōtra; and to Mallana of Kūvalli, son of Maṅgalayapa to Daṇḍunabali and Authala of the Āśvalāyana-sūtra, Kāśyapa-gōtra and Ṛik-śākhā. It is also stated that Tryaiṇ- haka divided, ārādhira and, after retaining a portion of it for himself, distributed the rest amongst a number of brāh- maṇas and a couple of dēvatas. The record was written by Vīraṇācārya, the son of Mallapa. Cf. Ep. Carn., Vol. VII, Sk. No. 26.

cells.place: contd. HYDERABAD DISTRICT—contd. Fragments lying in the same Office. Findspot: Ruined Śiva temple, Nidigonda, Jangaon Taluk, Warangal District.
cells.date: Śaka 1141 (chandra-abdhi-iśa), Rākta-kshi, Rāḍha (Radha), Jyeṣṭha śu. 6, Sunday=1210 A.D., April 21.
cells.remarks: Begins with the Kākatiya genealogy. Records (1) the erection of Trikūṭa temple for the deities such as Rudra, Mādhava-Mahādēva and another (name lost) and shrines for other deities such as Sūryadēva, Gaṇapati, etc., by Kuṇḍanāmba, the daughter of Mahādēva and the queen of Rudra, the Nāṭavāḍi chief and the provision made for worship etc., (2) the founding of Kundapura and its gift to Brāhmaṇas, (3) the construction of a temple for Śiva at Jijjikallu, (4) the gift of lamps for the two shrines of Ardhanārīśvara, Uṇḍanāhēśvara and Kuṇḍēśvara at the village Kālēśvara, Mantrakūṭa and Śrīkaila respectively and a tank called Kuṇḍasamudra.

cells.place: Slab lying outside the Śiva temple, front side.
cells.date: Śaka 1196, (wrong for 1180), Raktākshi, Jyeṣṭha śu. 5 Friday=1264 A.D., May 2.
cells.remarks: Records the consecration of the (image of the) deity Siddha-mahālakshmi for the welfare of the chief by Sukadēva. cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT / NALGONDA TALUK †
cells.place: Slab set up on the tankbund outside the village.
cells.date: Kali 4989, Saka 1810, Hijri 1306, Sarva- dhāri, Mārgaśīra śu. 10, Friday = 1858, A.D., December 28.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. The Telugu portion records the renovation of tank and construction of a new sluice at Pamugallu in Xindukala-sīma, and of a feeder canal from the dan to the tank called Udayasamudra and the arrangements made for the discharge of the excess waters to river Sīpāta through another channel by Sayidu Salār Mir by Rāmatulla. It also records the gift of the dasabandha ley on produce from the lands irrigated by the canal apportioned as follows; one share to the king, one and a half share to the people and two shares to the Tulukās and the Brahamaṇas. Published in Ep. Ind. XXX, pp. 23-25 and Plate XI a. For the Persian portion see App. D, No. 2.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH—concld. / NALGONDA DISTRICT—concld. / SURYAPET TALUK—concld. / Nâgulapâdu—concld. †
cells.place: Wall left of the doorway of the same temple.
cells.date:
1) Raktâkshi, Jyêshtha śu. 11, Thursday. 1303 A.D., May 1.
2) Kshaya, Phâlguna ba. 11, Monday, Prababhava = 1267 A.D., February 21
cells.remarks: The inscription in three sections engraved continuously records three grants given to god Ammâraśa, Tâttâ, enshrined at Narêśvara, Ayyâram and Kâlêśvara. The first section records the grant of *4 maruturus* of land as *vritti* under the canal from the Musi by Kâmaya, Nâmaya and Mallaya for the merit of their father Kat-rôdi and their mother Paramânam and mentions many details. The second section records the grant of 4 *maruturus* of land irrigated by the tank Nâmasamudra to the east of Nâgulapâdu Kâmaya for the merit of his parents and for his own merit on the date cited second. The third section records the grant of 2 *maruturus* of land under the tank Chidâla-cheruvu to the south of Pinadêvulapalli and 2 *maruturus* of land near the samo tank by Nâmaya for the merit of his parents and for his own merit also on the date cited second. Ibid. p. 95, No. Ng. 31.

cells.date: Regnal year 42, Chitrahānu, Māgha, Punnami, Sunday (?) and a Chandra-māna solar eclipse. Irregular.
cells.remarks: States that the chief was governing Kokaṇṇa-900 and Palasige-12,000 from his capital Gōva. Registers grants of wet-lands, for the purpose of renovation of the temple and daily offerings to god Sūlīśvara and for the feeding of the ascetics. Other 1 gifts are :--gadyāṇa-aigaṁda-kāri and aruvaṭt-okkalu of the place. The grants were made over to sthānāchārya Śambhudēva. It also records grants of income from baḍagāyu-ta[ga]re by suṅkaḍa-adhikāri and [tula]bhāra by [ka]mmatas, (tammatas ?), etc. of the kālu of the place, oisa per hēru etc., by Vaikamāha-setti-śāsinuru and also another gift by Sūmachamradraṇādhyaka, to the same deity.

cells.place: Biligi.—Slabs leaning against the wall in the Ratnatraya basti, No. 1.
cells.date:
(1) Śaka 1500, Vikāri, amāvāsya, śu. 5, Monday-1581 A.D., January 9. The Śaka year was current.
(2) Śaka 1510, Sarvajit, Caitra śu. 1, Nan-merated), made for the worship and maintenance, by the queen of the chief of Biligi, as stated in a postscript that on the date cited third Bāmādēvi, the queen of Ghaṇṭēndra constructed a gaṇḍahasti-basti for Śāntivāra and granted lands to provide for worship and maintenance, and gave grants to the temple at Koppala near Hale-Biligi for the milk-bath of Nēminātham.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the Ratnatraya-basti by Ratnapa, son of the minister of the wodeyars, Candra-śāla etc., and the installation of the images of Nēmināvara, Pārśvanātha and Vardhamāna by his son Ghaṇṭēndra on the advice of Bhaṭṭa-Akala on the date cited first and records the grants of land. The income of the basti was derived from the income from nine villages and lands yielding 300 khaṇḍugas of paddy and other several gifts (enumerated), made for the worship and maintenance, by the queen of the chief of Biligi, and a postscript that on the date cited third Bāmādēvi, the queen of Ghaṇṭēndra constructed a gaṇḍahasti-basti for Śāntivāra and granted lands to provide for worship and maintenance, and gave grants to the temple at Koppala near Hale-Biligi for the milk-bath of Nēminātham.

cells.location: Kānsūr
cells.place: Hero-stone standing near the Iśvara temple.
cells.date: Kāli 428[2], Plava, [Mā]gga śu. 12,000, Monday=1181 A.D., December 4
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that while mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kīrtidēva was ruling, [Banavāsi]-12,000 and [Hāngal]-500 who is the son of Bammara, died on behalf of the king Kādēva in a battle fought at Hubbase. Seems to record also the arrangement made by Perggaḍe Māmaliyāṇa and Perggaḍe Bīramma for the payment of some gadyāṇas as a religious house as compensation. [Mā]maliyāṇa and Parikāntadēva, Hasagali Kādēva and another Kādēva are stated to have taken part in the battle.

cells.location: Siddāpura †
cells.place: Tamadikalla. Hero-stone standing before the dilapidated temple.
cells.date: Saka 993, Viśāthi-kṛti, Āshādha śu. 5, Sunday=1071 A. D., June 9.
cells.remarks: Records the death of Śiṇṭayya-gauḍa of Śirehaṭṭi in the battle fought by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kīrttivarmma and his younger brother Chaṭṭayyādēva of the Kaḍamba family with Udayāditya, the governor of 12 villages who laid a siege to the fort of Banavāsi at the instance of the king. Kīrttivarmma is stated to have earned the displeasure of the king for establishing Permmādi (Vikramāditya VI) on the throne. The siege is stated to have been led by the hero's brother Chikkayya-gauḍa and his eldest son Barmmayya. Cf. Ibid., No. 3.

cells.location: Banavāsi. †
cells.place: 186 lying in the backyard of the house of Ma..n..gayya in the village. [Survey No. 423. Old Gaon Thana].
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Engraved bottom upwards. Starts with the praise of Vishnu and gives the natal genealogy. Mentions Kākusthavarmma and his son Śānti-varmma, the grandfather and father of the king respectively. Refers to the taking away of the glory of a certain monarch (name lost) who was the ruler of Kūṭṭūr, defeating the enemies, perhaps by Mṛigēśavarmma. Some broken parts of this pillar containing some phrases like Arjuna, sāmanta etc., are preserved in the district library at Dharwar. In characters of about the 5th century. Published in Epigraphia Karṇāṭaka, Vol. 52, Part I, pp. 25 ff. and Plate.

cells.location: Shimoga
cells.place: Slabs leaning against the outer wall of the District Museum, No. 1.
cells.date: (2) Śaka 1054, Nandana, Chaitra Puṇṇami, lunar eclipse, Sunday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Contains the genealogy of the Gaṅga family and an account of their prowess. Records that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Gaṅga-Permmāḍidēva was ruling over the province of Hoysala-king Ereyanga, ruling over Ededore-1000 from his residence at Harige, caused the construction of a chaityālaya in the village, and on the second date, of a village (the name not clear) along with its income for the upkeep of the expenses of repairs and maintenance. Records also that the gift of the village of the Gaṅga-jinālaya at Kuruḷya-tīrtha by Satya-gaṅga and the grant, on the second date, of a village (name not clear) after having purchased it from the receptor Mādhava-chandradēva. Records also the gift of the village, made by Kāliyara Malli-seṭṭi after purchasing it from heggade Chaṇḍimayya, the subordinate of Hermmāḍidēva, to Mādhava-chandradēva. Published in Ep. Carn., Vol. VII, Shimoga No. 64.

cells.location: Shimoga
cells.place: Slabs leaning against the outer wall of the District Museum.
cells.date: (1) Śaka 1029[o], Sarvadhāri, Phālguna [10], Friday=1108 A.D., March 2. (2) Śaka 1043, Subhakṛit, Bhādrapada śu. 5, Thursday=1122 A.D., August 13. The week-day was Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Gōṅga kings down to Nanniya-Gaṅga and records the gift of a village of the village of the Krāṇur-gāvu. Records the grant of the village Heggaṇale and lands inside the tank at Harakēri by the chief and also the endowment of the income of one village of the village of the same name to the temple of Pāṭṭada-tirtha-basadi at 3. P. 1043, a dīvige-gift to P.bhāndār siddhāntadēva who is stated to have owned the construction of 25 chaityālayas including the Kuḍiya-basadi. Gifts were also recorded to have been given to the above basadi by Kichchiga in the reign of Nanniya-Gaṅga at the time of the birth of their son Hammāḍi-dēva. The latter is stated to have caused the Pāṭṭada-tirtha-basadi to be constructed of stone. Ibīḍ., Shimoga, No. 4.

cells.remarks: Mentions Virūpākṣa-daṇṇāyaka, son of Mahāpradhāna Bukkappa-daṇṇāyaka as ruling over Bairākūru-rājya. Records that the old basadi of Haṭṭiyaṅgaḍi was burnt and the record which was stated to have been destroyed, was restored in the past by fire, by getting it engraved in a concise form in small stones to be preserved in the central shrine. The grant was made by Bukkappa-mahārāya to Candranāthācārya gives a detailed account of the bene-actions (dharma) assigned for various services to the deity Candranāthasvāmi of the basadi at Haṭṭiyaṅgaḍi.

cells.place: Stone slab built into the wall of a ruined structure known as Mātākī-śāl close to the site called Khāku-dēvī-lān.
cells.date: Vikrama 918, Chaitra śu. 2, Wednesday, Hasta-nakshatra. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the ruler. The praśasti portion refers to the founding of a market at the village of Rohiṁsakūpa and to the creation of two pillars, one at Maḍyōdara and the other at Rōhiṁsakūpa by the ruler, for the increase of his fame. Records that he caused to be built a temple of the god Jina and that in a meeting the Gōṣṭhīs of the Mahājanas (gōṭhī-gōṭhī) presided over by the ascetics Jamva (Jāṁ-bava?) and Amvaya (Āmaka?) and the merchant Bhāṇḍa (Bhākuṭa?) in the gachchha of Dhānesvara (Dhanēśvara). Published in JRAS, 1895, pp. 513-21; Bhandarkar's List, No. 31.

cells.place: Śrīkṣētra. Nine fragments of an inscribed stone discovered during excavations. Impressions received from Shri Aung Thaw, Director, Archaeolo-gical Survey of Burma, Rangoon.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. The first fragment mentions a Kalasōpu-rēśvara (name lost) born of a queen, probably Bhaṭṭa-Dēvī-dēvī. Fragment 2 mentions two persons who are compared to the sun and the moon and refers to a monastery (mahā-vihāra) built probably to a stūpa. The aforesaid Kalasōpurē-śvara is also mentioned. Fragment 3 refers to a king, Hōṭṭivi, a certain Dharmadāsa of (?) Kalasōpura and a person named Yajñadēva (or Yachadēva ?). Fragment 4 describes two persons and contains the name Yajña (?). The remain-ing five fragments do not contain anything of importance. In characters of about the 8th century.

cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records that Sayyid Shāh Mīr Iṣfahānī, son of Sayyid Aḥmad Ṭabāṭabā'ī, carried out repairs to the dam of the tank, which had been long desolate, for his merit. The work was supervised by Rai Chintāman, son of Pandit Karīm Khwānjahā'ī. Further states that the lands starting from the embankment of river Mushī Indaraparaḷ to the bank of the river Krishnā, which are irrigated by the canal tank and pond, and situated within the qasba Pāngal, and the lands irrigated by the dam, the Mumilā and the king and the Hindus have a two-two share. Cf. Ep. In. Mos., 1925-26, pp. 23-24, pl. XI a. For the Telugu version, see no. 46 of Appendix B.

cells.place: Indore.—Copper plates in the possession of Dr. S.N. Nagn, No. I. (Impressions received from the Chief Epigraphist, Mysore).
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records the grant of Mad land, measuring ten bighas situated in the vicinity of the village Nāgadī, pargana Mān-Khera, between Bhinjī and Jārībī (?) the Pawāne (Pawār) Rājputs, residents of Jāora. It further states that may dig up a new well in it with an adda on payment of an annual revenue of rupees fifty Sālamshāhī (i.e. Shāh 'Alam Shāhī) at the rate of rupees five per bigha, without fail. Further stipulates that the said land shall be inherited after proper measurement and the chakbandī may be entrusted to the said donees who are exhorted to take to their avocations in all tranquility. Written on the date quoted. For Nāgarī portion, see No. 9 of Appendix A.

cells.remarks: Do. cells.place: No. 5. Do.
cells.remarks: Do. Records the grant of 30 bighas of tax-free land described as fallow but cultivable, situated in the vicinity of village Bhimā Kheri, pargana Jjora, to Akhūnzāda Muhammad Ahmad, son of Akhūnzāda Muhammad 'Uthman Şahib, perpetually for planting an orchard. cells.location: INDORE DISTRICT INDORE TAHASIL †
cells.place: No. 6. Do.
cells.remarks: Do. Records that the present and future Mutasaddis of pargana Baranda, a suburb of sarkar Gulshanābād alias Jaora state that 25 bighas of tax-free land comprising 10 bighas of Mal land and 15 bighas of fallow but cultivable land, situated on the road to Bar-Khera, in the vicinity of the qasba Baranda has been donated perpetually to Bhagwandas and Chhitman, son of Beni Rām, of Nagdā, Brahmins, residents of the aforesaid qasba, for sinking a well, garden and cultivation. The aforesaid persons have full liberty either to plant a flower-garden or mango orchard or to cultivate the donated land. The Mutasaddis should not demand rent from the grantee-proprietor after every measurement and chakhbandi and should not insist on a new sanad every year. Even when needed, trees grown in the aforesaid land shall not be cut and carried for Government uses, nor any grazing tax shall be levied for the animals with in any way. The Mutasaddis should treat it as a warsi inand act accordingly. Written on the date quoted For the Nāgarī portion, see No. 14 of Appendix A.

Records that the present and future Mutasaddis of pargana Baranda, a suburb of sarkar Gulshanābād alias Jaora state that 25 bighas of tax-free land comprising 10 bighas of Mal land and 15 bighas of fallow but cultivable land, situated on the road to Bar-Khera, in the vicinity of the qasba Baranda has been donated perpetually to Bhagwandas and Chhitman, son of Beni Rām, of Nagdā, Brahmins, residents of the aforesaid qasba, for sinking a well, garden and cultivation. The aforesaid persons have full liberty either to plant a flower-garden or mango orchard or to cultivate the donated land. The Mutasaddis should not demand rent from the grantee-proprietor after every measurement and chakhbandi and should not insist on a new sanad every year. Even when needed, trees grown in the aforesaid land shall not be cut and carried for Government uses, nor any grazing tax shall be levied for the animals with in any way. The Mutasaddis should treat it as a warsi inand act accordingly. Written on the date quoted For the Nāgarī portion, see No. 14 of Appendix A.
